title: Tuxedos, ball jobs and deceased bandmates
summary: He tells of dressing the band in tuxedos, hiring for balls and pay disputes, then discusses black and white locals and New York's 802.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Right there. And the other thing was jaffy. We didn't know what jazz was down here. We went there. We called ourselves a ragtime band. To the rock around there, they called them the Nick LaRocca and jazz band. But before they first worked, there was the Dixieland band. They added the name jazz to it. They worked at the Shilla Cafe at a while. Of course you knew, some guy in New York made them a big oven and went to the Palais Royal. There ain't no more Palais Royal in New York now, but that's where they went from. They went to the Palais Royal. They hired class to you. They all had a black tuxedo with button cloth top shoes on. I didn't like that man. They used to wear the cloth top button shoes with the tuxedo. I used to have a pair of them. Man, we was around Chicago. We went to the Florida. When we first went up there, everybody bought spats. Pearl gray top shoes and black bottoms. Then we bought spats to put on. When we first started to wear tuxedos, we got a job down in Pensacola. Everybody had a tuxedo. Marcus Corn used to play baritone with me in the brass band. He's dead now. He's a good musician. He was the one who teach my brother how to play alto on. Marcus went and borrowed all those tuxedos. He was on the Royal Coyle and was out of style. He put them on the tuxedos and just the tuxedos in. We come back and we all had to get tuxedos now. We went over to Canal Street, the one of them clothes. I did what it was. Nobody had any money. I had to stand credit for the whole band for the five tuxedos. I'd fit the whole band with tuxedos. We had to go play them big dances. You had tuxedos, see? I'll never forget one night that I had to play a ball at the... I think it was the... Or the Bahamian or Hermes. I wasn't supposed to play in the band. I was supposed to put the band directly. See? I always met the band still having eight or ten bands. I used to hire a lot of fellas out of the symphony. Paul Casaborn, the timpani's and stuff like that. And frankly, I had to have a rent off. One of these full-dressed sussies with a lot of tuxedos. Well, I'll tell you a lot. Well, I go, they come home and I'm laughing like the tail came off. It looked like I had a dinner jacket on there. I was going to have to play the supper dance at the... I believe it was the John Hotel up there. I was still around there with that thing. He put a... He had a paper that actually had rented the soup for me. What a mind. All I had was the pants from the tuxedos. Quoting the white tie. I never forget that night. They all come over there from the... From the ball. They come over there and put this high hat on. John Lampers, he's a liar. And I watch them. You were working some of that guy? He come in and I'll grab them with a cigar on his top hat. And he looked like Flip coming in there. I laughed that night and I said, All you need now John is a green face and you'll be fixed up. We played that dance and we went to play... Old Sweet Home. Some of that stuff, I was a man going to play Old Sweet Home. All right. And that hour, so much for that hour. 55 hours. Well... And I said, all right, go ahead and play. And add it to the contract. All right. A little while after, another guy comes running along and says, How much for that hour? I said, $54. He's there. Give me $54. Never $55. At the jungle town. I'm a big gambling guy. Moving, grunting, you know what I mean? That's a $55 too. Another time we was playing as a... Well, it was a postmaster. He was the captain of the club. At the roost club. He got drunk all up and dancing around. He knocked the music stand. He knocked everything off. He goes down his pocket. He went to paper and everything. And you look at some daughter, was the queen of that boy. I'll never forget that. And he said to me, he said, How do you stop intermissions? Go eat something. Don't stop your having a good time. I said, get for us to eat after something. I'll pick you up. So, we kept on playing until after it got through. Nobody wanted to stay. All the guys were wrapping up their stuff and putting it in their pocket. Taking it home with it. And then we could get five dollars to play piano with them. You know what I mean? He had that in the mouth. He had a lot of clock popped up. He had a lot of clock popped up. He had a lot of clock popped up. He had a lot of clock popped up. He had a lot of clock popped up. Yeah. Yeah. Bob Aguilar is dead, isn't he? Oh yeah, he's dead. His dead, Dennis Daniel is dead. Brother Dan Taggart died. Dan Taggart died? Yeah, Harold Shannon died. Oshir Bakay died about two years ago in Venice, California. He went over there and stayed in California. Where he's got two boys who made good musicians. One of the boys playing best singing in San Francisco or Los Angeles, one of them symphonies. Little Paul in Detroit told me he was in town about a year ago. He told me that Bakay died and he was telling me about his sons and made good musicians. They go as white people out there, I guess. Out there, I guess so. I really don't know. But out there, that local is all in one colored and white all in the game, you see. They say, well, in Florida, they ain't got no white colored local down there, so I wonder. Yeah. It's got different colored locals in different states, you see. New York, I don't know where they got a white colored local. They only got 802. Somebody told me there was a colored union up there, but when I got up there, they had colored, last year I was up there. 802. And I went back in 802. I was in 802 in 1924. Yeah. And I went back in. And of course, they have to put you before the board of directors and they had Negroes on the board of directors up there. That's what I'm telling you. That's why I said I knew where they had them. I don't know whether that's a general practice or whether...
